title: Progressive onboarding
summary: Teach only the concepts needed to reach first value, then reveal advanced guidance in context instead of front-loading a product tour.
problem: Long onboarding tours delay value and are forgotten before users reach the features being explained.
use_when: The product has unfamiliar concepts but users can learn them while doing real tasks
Advanced features are not required for first success
avoid_when: Safety, compliance, or irreversible consequences require instruction before use
The product is so simple that onboarding adds friction
rationale: Contextual learning is easier to connect to a real goal.
First-use guidance should disappear or remain dismissible after it has served its purpose.

use_if: The product has unfamiliar concepts but users can learn them while doing real tasks
Advanced features are not required for first success
prefer_alternatives_if: Users must understand critical safety or compliance information before acting

requirements: Do not make tutorials pointer-gesture dependent.
Keep dismiss or skip actions reachable and clearly named.
Avoid auto-advancing content before users can read it.
Identify the earliest meaningful user success.
Teach only what is needed to reach it.
Move advanced guidance to the context where the feature appears.
